title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page: S is a base on which 2 is invertible, and X/S is an elliptic curve with extra structure (written omega_X). Legendre theory X -> X/{±1} (as I read it) turns this into the following data:
- an S_3-torsor T, equivalently the finite étale degree-3 cover S'/S;
- the twisted line Y = T ∧_{S_3} P^1_S, with S' = T ∧_{S_3} {0,1,∞};
- a section e of U = Y − S'.
So U is a twisted form of M_{0,4} = P^1 − {0,1,∞}, and e plays the role of the Legendre parameter λ.

U embeds canonically into J^0_{U/S}, the twisted form of the generalized Jacobian of P^1 with modulus 0+1+∞ (formula 319). This is a rank-2 S-torus whose lattice is built from M_0(S'/S), the degree-zero divisors supported on S'. Untwisted, the embedding is essentially t ↦ (t, 1−t) into G_m^2.

Grothendieck first notes that this embedding should be made explicit in terms of standard 'elliptic functions'. He declines to do so and turns to the point e ∈ U(S) ⊂ H^0(S, J^0_{U/S}) (320). He crosses out a first attempt (a map H^0(S, J^0) -> H). Instead he uses the tower of multiplication-by-n isogenies (321): 1 -> _nJ^0 -> J^0 -> J^0 -> 1, for n variable. Passing to the projective limit gives the universal pro-isogeny (322):
- 1 -> T_∞(J^0) -> \tilde J^0 -> J^0 -> 1, where \tilde J^0 = lim_n J^0;
- p denotes the map \tilde J^0 -> J^0;
- T_∞(J^0) ≅ T_∞(G_m)_S ⊗_Z M_0(S'/S).
The fibre p^{-1}(e) is a T_∞(J^0)-torsor; concretely, the torsor of compatible systems of n-th roots of the coordinates (λ, 1−λ).

Formula (323), via (30') on p. 719', identifies this torsor with F_∞(\tilde X/S). That object is defined on p. 719'; from context it is the profinite 'fibre at infinity' or level-structure torsor attached to the profinite tower over X.

The following page continues the argument:
- The class of the torsor is the Kummer image of e under the coboundary H^0(S, J^0) -> H^1(S, T_∞ J^0).
- The kernel of that map is the infinitely divisible elements.
- For S reduced of finite type over Z this kernel vanishes, since the groups of units are finitely generated.
- Hence the 'original elliptic' section e, i.e. the curve X, is determined by this Galois-theoretic profinite torsor.

The purpose is the anabelian programme of the Longue Marche: recovering elliptic curves (and the λ-line) from Kummer-type torsors of profinite coverings, via the arithmetic of M_{0,4}.
errors: Possible duality slip: the cocharacter lattice of the generalized Jacobian G_m^3/G_m is Z^3/Z, the dual of the degree-zero lattice. As S_3-modules over Z these may differ at the prime 3. So T_∞(J^0) ≅ T_∞(G_m) ⊗ M_0(S'/S) is correct only if M_0 is meant in the dual sense, or after inverting 3. The conventions of p. 720 are not visible here, so this is unsure.

The 'canonical' S_3-equivariant embedding U -> J^0 needs care. Untwisted, t ↦ (t, 1−t) is equivariant only up to translation by the sign −1: e.g. 1/t gives (t^{-1}, −(1−t)t^{-1}). Strictly the target is a Pic^1-type torsor, or equivariance holds only modulo 2-torsion. Grothendieck asserts canonicity without addressing this, though 2 is invertible on S.
The 'elliptic functions' explicitation of the morphism X -> J^0 is announced and then explicitly skipped (a gap he acknowledges, not an error).

ideas.what: Twisted generalized Jacobian of P^1 minus a degree-3 étale divisor S' as a rank-2 torus with lattice M_0(S'/S), with the Legendre λ-line embedded in it
ideas.modern_name: generalized Jacobian / torus of units of M_{0,4}, twisted by an S_3-torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rosenlicht–Serre (generalized Jacobians); the twisting is standard descent

ideas.what: Universal pro-isogeny \tilde J = lim_n J and the fibre over a section as a T_∞-torsor (Kummer torsor)
ideas.modern_name: Kummer map H^0(S,G) -> H^1(S, T_∞ G) / profinite Kummer theory for tori
ideas.where_published: related material in SGA 4 / Grothendieck's letters (unsure)

ideas.what: Identifying a profinite torsor attached to the elliptic curve (F_∞(\tilde X/S)) with the Kummer torsor of the Legendre parameter (λ, 1−λ) in the twisted torus
ideas.modern_name: Kummer classes of λ, 1−λ governing the Galois action on 2-power and other torsion of Legendre curves; Kummer-theoretic reconstruction in anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: partly folklore (2-descent, Legendre / 2-division fields); Kummer-theoretic reconstruction later systematised by Nakamura and Mochizuki

ideas.what: Injectivity of the Kummer map on sections of a torus over a reduced base of finite type over Z, so the elliptic curve is determined by its Kummer torsor
ideas.modern_name: injectivity of Kummer map (no divisible units over finitely generated bases)

missed.claim: Grothendieck frames the Legendre elliptic curve's profinite 'fibre at infinity' torsor as the pullback, along the λ-section, of the universal pro-isogeny of the generalized Jacobian of the twisted P^1−{0,1,∞}. Combined with the next page, this means the elliptic curve is recovered from the Kummer class of (λ, 1−λ). This is an early anabelian 'Kummer reconstruction' viewpoint linking M_{1,1}[2] and M_{0,4}.
missed.quote: on a (cf (30') p. 719') F_∞(\tilde X/S) ≃ p^{-1}(e), le T_∞(J^0_{U/S})-torseur déduit de la section e
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates the systematic use of Kummer classes of units on M_{0,4} in anabelian geometry (Nakamura; Mochizuki's Kummer theory). It is mostly a precursor rather than a new result.

missed.claim: Explicit description of the canonical morphism X -> J^0_{U/S} in terms of standard elliptic functions was announced but skipped.
missed.quote: on a à expliciter en termes de "fonctions elliptiques" standard. Sans m'attarder sur une telle explicitation
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor, classical computation (Legendre / Jacobi formulas); low value.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard Kummer theory applied to the twisted generalized Jacobian of P^1−{0,1,∞}. The only distinctive point is using it to tie an elliptic curve's profinite torsor to the Kummer class of λ in an anabelian frame, and that is largely anticipated by later published work.
transcription_corrections: Equation numbers, consistent with (318) on the previous page and (324) on the next, are (319) for U ↪ J^0_{U/S} and (320) for e ∈ U(S)=H^0(S,J^0_{U/S}). The crossed-out map H^0(S,J^0)->H is (321). The isogeny tower is (321) after renumbering, the universal isogeny is (322), and F_∞(\tilde X/S) ≃ p^{-1}(e) is (323). They are not (31), (31'), (32), (32'), (32'').
'et à la section unique' is better read as 'et à la section ...' (word uncertain; possibly 'canonique' or 'unique').
In (322) the isomorphism T_∞(J^0_{U/S}) ≅ T_∞(G_m)_S ⊗_Z M_0(S'/S) is written vertically below T_∞(J^0). The definition \tilde J^0_{U/S} =def lim_{←, n} (J^0_{U/S}) is written below \tilde J^0.
The page number at top is 724; the archive page number is 152.
